2. [ASSISTANT_SAID] CDP's framework can be used in conjunction with other reporting frameworks, such as GRI, SASB, TCFD, and IR, to provide more comprehensive reporting on an organization's climate-related impacts, risks, and opportunities.

5. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) proposes a new standardized reporting format for sustainability information to be included in annual reports.
6. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The proposed format is based on the European Single Electronic Format (ESEF), which is already used for financial reporting in the EU.
7. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The ESEF format requires companies to use Inline XBRL (eXtensible Business Reporting Language) when preparing their annual reports.
8. [ASSISTANT_SAID] XBRL is a global standard for exchanging business information and has been widely adopted for financial reporting.
9. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The proposed format for sustainability reporting under the CSRD aims to make sustainability information more comparable and accessible for investors and stakeholders.
10. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The format is expected to be introduced in 2024, with reporting required from 2026 onwards.
11. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Non-Financial Reporting Directive (NFRD) does not prescribe a particular format for reporting.
12. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The NFRD requires companies to report relevant non-financial information in their management reports or in a separate sustainability report.
13. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The information to be disclosed under NFRD includes a description of the company's business model, policies, outcomes, risks, and impacts related to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues.
14. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The European Commission has encouraged the use of internationally recognized reporting frameworks and standards, such as GRI, SASB, and TCFD, to ensure that the information disclosed is relevant, reliable, and comparable.
